subject: Realtime metering spike and overage - Jun 14
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@arcadia.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@arcadia.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 09:12:00 +0100
Subject: Unexpected real-time metering spike (06/14) - urgent billing hold request

Hi Chloe,

We're seeing a large metering spike in our June 14 usage that generated a ~€12,400 overage on the June invoice. I've attached a small usage snapshot (usage_snapshot_20280614.csv) showing a concentrated burst between 22:00-23:15 CEST that we don't recognize.

This request is urgent because our finance team has placed the invoice on hold until we get a root cause — we need a line-by-line attribution (request ids / model variants / region) and clarification on VAT handling for any disputed portion. Arcadia is an EU entity (we expect reverse-charge treatment in most cases) — please confirm what you need from us (VAT ID, billing entity) so we can get the correct tax treatment.

Two additional notes:
- We did run an internal prefetch job the evening of the 14th for a holiday campaign, but our devs believe the test cluster should have been filtered out at the client side. The spike still looks like production scale.
- Please advise whether Redwood can provisionally pause collection on the disputed amount while you investigate.

I've CC'd our billing alias for records. We can share logs on a drive link if needed (see attached zip).

Thanks,
Sofia Ramos
Head of Platform, Arcadia AI
sofia@arcadia.ai

Attachments: usage_snapshot_20280614.csv, arcadia_testcluster_logs_20280614.zip

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@arcadia.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, billing@arcadia.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 11:30:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected real-time metering spike (06/14) - urgent billing hold request

Hi Sofia — thanks for the heads up and for the snapshot.

I'll coordinate an immediate triage with Billing Ops and our Observability team. To help speed this up, can you also send:
- A sample of request IDs (5–10) from the time window you flagged, ideally with full request timestamps and the client IPs (or trace IDs).
- Confirmation whether the prefetch job used the same API keys as production or a dedicated test key.

Action plan (short):
1) Kimberly will pull the token-level ledger and match request IDs to model variants and region.
2) Ben will ask Engineering to look for duplicate counting and border-case prefix caching that can inflate counts.
3) I'll open a provisional billing review and put a temporary hold on collection for the disputed line while we run the forensic (pending approval by Collections).

If you can share the additional logs / request ids by EOD today we'll aim to get a first-pass breakdown within 24 hours.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai, Sofia Ramos <sofia@arcadia.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 13:02:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected real-time metering spike (06/14) - quick troubleshooting notes

Hey team — quick note from Sales/CS side:

If Arcadia ran a large prefetch job, two common outcomes we see that look like "surges":
- Client-side prefetch using a production API key and not tagging with a test prefix, so requests are billed as normal.
- A misconfigured retry loop in client code that multiplies identical requests (shows up as repeated request ids if dedup isn't applied).

Kimberly / Observability: can you flag whether the requests in the snapshot share identical prompt hashes or request ids? If so, we can often map this to a retry pattern.

From a commercial perspective, happy to support a provisional credit if the forensic points to a client-side mis-keying. We'll need to agree on a simple reconciliation window and amount.

Ben
Account Executive — Enterprise
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@arcadia.ai>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: billing@arcadia.ai
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 15:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected real-time metering spike (06/14) - additional logs attached

Thanks Chloe — attaching our server logs for the time window (arcadia_testcluster_logs_20280614.zip). The prefetch job used key pref- live-032 (we thought the client sandbox would strip it but apparently the same key was used).

We've also attached a short CSV with 8 request ids we can reproduce from our test cluster. Please let me know if you can match these to your ledger.

On VAT: Arcadia's EU VAT ID is EU-ARCADIA-5543 — can you confirm if Redwood will reissue the disputed portion as reverse-charge or if the original invoice will require an adjustment? Our accounting team is ready to open a VAT reclaim if needed.

We would appreciate a temporary pause on collection for the disputed amount until the forensic completes.

Regards,
Sofia

Attachments: arcadia_testcluster_logs_20280614.zip

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@arcadia.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, billing@arcadia.ai
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 17:03:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Unexpected real-time metering spike (06/14) - next steps and provisional credit

Sofia — quick update after the initial review:

What we found so far (first-pass):
- The request ids you sent map to a concentrated set of request hashes that were billed under Arcadia's production key.
- Traces show repeated identical prompt payloads within the same minute window and high concurrency from a small set of client IPs — consistent with a prefetch job using the production key rather than a test key.
- There's an indication of duplicate counting for the first-token in a small subset due to a retry loop in the client (we've opened a ticket with Eng, INC-7119).

VAT / invoicing:
- To proceed with reverse-charge reissuance we need Arcadia's formal VAT registration docs and confirmation of the billing entity. Kimberly will follow up with the exact fields required.

Provisional commercial resolution:
- Collections has approved a provisional 50% credit on the disputed overage (€6,200) pending the full forensic (expected 48–72 hours). We'll hold collection on the disputed line for now.
- If engineering confirms client-side mis-keying / retry multiplication, we will apply a retroactive adjustment and reissue the invoice net of VAT per the reconciliation. If the spike is shown to be legitimate production usage, the provisional credit will be reversed and we will proceed with normal collection.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Kimberly to confirm required VAT docs (within 4 business hours).
2) Observability + Eng to deliver token-level reconciliation and sample traces (24–72 hours).
3) Finance to post provisional credit and update invoice status (within 24 hours).

I'll attach a provisional calculation we used for the credit (provisional_credit_calc_20280615.xlsx) and have updated the invoice record with a 'disputed' flag.

If you can send the VAT registration PDF and the full list of offending request ids, that will speed this up.

Best,
Chloe
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
chloe.martin@redwood.ai

Attachments: provisional_credit_calc_20280615.xlsx, invoice_20280601.pdf
